labels.label: bbsrem:degk
labels.notes: Unmarked, row partial: right, because the second sentence (l.1335-1336, the AdS wedge) waits on T-bbs-q8 and the first is read at the link and HS levels. The assembly GX.bbsrem_degk_link_hs (HSDegree.lean:1896) is at least the paper's first sentence in the named readings. Hypotheses: 0 <= Q(C.pt) is weaker than p in dS^2. Degree 2k is f = delta^{2k} g with g having a fixed point and k >= 1 (l.739, l.905; one turn of l(p) is delta^2, OQ-113 (b)). The hyperbolic type is not assumed. theta is oriented, which is the paper's own canonical orientation (l.729-731, l.770), not an added hypothesis; the cover theorems take any theta. Conclusion: L_1 at the same p with lifted holonomy delta^2 g_1 (g_1 has a fixed point, g_1^k = g), so degree 2. pr : L -> L_1 is a k-sheeted covering map (Nat.card of each fibre is k) and a (Gamma_p, l(p))-morphism with pr(E' s) = E_1(k s), where C has the lifted pair (E', D_1(k .)). The type is kept both ways at dS^2 and at Q = 0, and the four signs are kept both ways. For every developing datum Delta_1 of L_1, the pulled-back Delta of L makes BiSusp.map pr : e(L) -> e(L_1) an HS-morphism (SingularHSStructure.IsMorphism, a non-vacuous morphism analogue of the strict IsIso) and a gx GX.IsBranchedCovering (gx's own GX/Branched/Basic.lean notion, not an ad hoc one), possibly branched over the apices, with branchingLocus = poles for k >= 2, k-to-one off the apices and one-to-one over each. The hypotheses are satisfiable: exists_spacelike_degree_two_mul builds positive and negative witnesses at every p in dS^2 and every k >= 1, with g hyperbolic. The three readings of 'can be constructed as' are each proved: exists_degree_two_cover, exists_kfold_cover_of_degree_two (at every p) and the existence of both signs. Readings disclosed in SCOPE (a)-(c) and in REPORT questions: k-branched cover in gx's sense, 'constructed as', and e(L) for the pulled-back Delta only (OQ-126 (c)). Positive/negative uses the l.915 form (OQ-120 (c)) with i^pm in the time-like reading (OQ-116 (a)). OQ-124 is not used, rightly: no isomorphism class is involved.

labels.notes: Unmarked, row partial: right. The printed sentence (l.1467-1469) is only the AdS wedge construction (T-bbs-q8), so the link and HS content is a reading: the light-like case of bbsrem:degk, disclosed in docstring l.23-27 and in the REPORT question. Covered by the same assembly at Q(C.pt) = 0, which includes both components of boundary H^2_pm; the k-th root is a null rotation, GX.GammaP.exists_eq_nullBoost and exists_pow_eq. GX.isParabolic_pow_iff keeps the type. GX.exists_lightlike_degree_two_mul gives 'one can construct light-like singularities of any degree 2k': positive and negative light-like (Gamma_p, l(p))-circles of every degree 2k at every light-like p, g parabolic with a fixed point, theta oriented.

findings.what: The 'Main declarations (all proved)' heading and the docstring of GX.GammaP.exists_pow_eq say 'Γ_p ≅ ℝ'. The file proves that every element of Γ_p is dsBoost ζ, resp. nullBoost s (exists_eq_dsBoost, exists_eq_nullBoost), and that these are homomorphisms from ℝ (…_add). That makes Γ_p a homomorphic image of ℝ. Injectivity is not proved. The statement is true and the REPORT's finding phrases it correctly ('the image of a one-parameter group').
findings.fix: Write 'Γ_p is the image of the one-parameter group ℝ (boosts, resp. null rotations)' in both places, or prove injectivity.

findings.what: The checklist row for « space-like singularity » / « light-like » is marked ✓ (carried). The assembly and the cover theorems assume only 0 ≤ Q(p), less than p ∈ dS² or Q(p) = 0, which kb/0006 marks '⚠ weakened'. The REPORT itself records this hypothesis as 'weakened'. The two disagree only in the mark; neither overclaims.
findings.fix: Mark the row '⚠ weakened: 0 ≤ Q(p) (space-like and light-like at once); the type and sign clauses at C.pt ∈ dS², resp. Q(C.pt) = 0'.

findings.what: The docstring of GX.exists_kfold_cover_regular ends '…the k-fold cover of a regular point's link, not of a singular one'. The theorem proves the first half. The second half (no k-fold covering of a singular degree-2 circle) is true: (δ²g₁)^k conjugate to δ^{2k} forces g₁^k = 1, hence g₁ = 1 by GTilde.eq_one_of_pow_eq_one. But the theorem does not state it.
findings.fix: Add '(argued)' after 'not of a singular one', or drop the clause.

report_check: The REPORT is final, not a draft. It was written at 09:13, after the last edit of the Lean file (09:11:48) and its olean (09:12:09). Its line references are correct: assembly at l.1896, SCOPE (a)-(e), sorry wording at l.10-11. Its 137-declaration count reproduces. Every listed declaration exists. Its hypotheses, sorries (none) and statuses (both partial, both unmarked) match the file. The three bbsrem:degk findings are true. (1) l.795 and l.798 do say Γ_p is 'generated by' a hyperbolic, resp. parabolic, element. The remark needs k-th roots in Γ_p, which a cyclic group would not supply, and GX.GammaP.exists_eq_dsBoost, exists_eq_nullBoost and exists_pow_eq formalize what OQ-122 (a) only argued. (2) With g = 1 the base has lifted holonomy δ², and the degree-2k cover of l(p) is neither hyperbolic nor parabolic. GX.exists_kfold_cover_regular builds the cover that GX.regular_not_isHyperbolic's docstring calls 'argued, not built'. (3) For k ≥ 2 the cover is branched exactly at the apices (susp_kfold_branched_cover). The light-like finding is true as well. The four questions each name their reading and are sound. OQ-120 (c), OQ-116 (a), OQ-126 (c) and OQ-113 (b) are cited where they bear. The 'package' field holds the target id, which is the campaign directory's name. The kb proposals are in the REPORT only: kb entries 0118-0123 come from the master's integration of T-bbs-positive-hs-surface, not from this closer.
